newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua says fire shuts belt at export terminal.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua says fire shuts belt at export terminal.

text.p: Brazil's key port of Paranagua said a fire at its export terminal had shut down one of five conveyor belts used for loading soybeans, a port official said.
"There was a fire at the conveyor belt which forms part of the export terminal," the official said. "The belt leaves the vertical soybean silo and enters the port."
The fire occurred at 2045 local (2345 GMT) on Monday. The cause was still under investigation, the official said.
The conveyor belt is one of a total five at the grain-loading export terminal. The port owns another three and a fourth belongs to Cargill.
"We have started the job of changing this conveyor belt, we have a spare one. In 10 days, maximum, the belt should be replaced," the official said.
All the other conveyor belts were currently functioning normally so that the port was working at four fifths of its normal loading capacity, he added.
